RESPONSIBILITY FOR HANDLING DRAINAGE COMPLAINTS
brainage complaints for highways under State maintenance shall be handled by the Bureau of Maintenance in each district except in those instances where the complaint has originated immediately after construction and prior to the acceptance of the improvement. In such cases the Bureaus of Construction and Design are responsible for analyzing the problem and recommending a solution. For highways not under State maintenance, complaints shall be referred to other appropriate highway authorities.
Since it is sometimes difficult to determine the original conditions of the drainage system after a highway building program has been completed, it is desirable that vertical aerial mapping photography be obtained prior to major construction or realignment and additional photography where needed after completion of construction. These photographs will provide documented evidence of before and after conditions which will justify a recommended course of action for any complaint made against the State. If it is determined that the Division is responsible, corrective action shall be taken.
RIGHTS TO NATURAL FLOW OF SURFACE WATERS
Scope
Surface drainage shall provide for the interception and disposal of rainwater and snow melt originating on the highway surface and immediate adjacent overlying areas. It shall be adequate to keep the pavement, but not necessarily the shoulders of the highway, passable by vehicular traffic. All roadway drainage, including side and slope ditches, shall be carried to a suitable outlet, preferably an existing stream. Where outletting to an existing stream is impractical or where no stream is available, appropriate drainage rights must be obtained.
Under drainage law as adopted in the State of Illinois, the owner of the dominant land has the right for surface waters coming or falling onto his land to pass off his land onto the servient land in the natural course of drainage. These principles apply when one tract of land is at a higher elevation than the adjoining land and thereby allows water to flow from the higher to lower land.
